planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Burkwood viburnum blooms on old wood, so prune only right after flowering.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Burkwood viburnum is a hybrid between Korean spice viburnum and service viburnum, combining the intense, spicy-sweet fragrance of its Korean parent with more vigorous growth, glossier foliage, and better heat tolerance, opening rounded clusters of pink buds that fade to white in early to mid spring. Its foliage is semi-evergreen in milder climates, holding dark green leaves through much of winter before dropping, and turning attractive burgundy-red in fall where it does go fully deciduous. The rounded, multi-stemmed shrub makes an excellent specimen near an entrance or window where its fragrance can be appreciated, or massed as a flowering screen. Prune lightly immediately after bloom to maintain shape, since later pruning removes the following year's flower buds.
